title.narrative: Emergency Response to the Returnees Crisis in Upper Nile State

description.narrative:
It is very important to intervene now because, as the emergency continues, people who fled the conflict in Sudan have lost all belongings and require basic human needs in order to survive, among which are food, shelter and to support resettle them once the returnees reach their home areas, for instance Fashoda county.
The overall objective of this project is to provide lifesaving assistance to the returnees and help them in South Sudan in a dignified way, with their basic humanitarian needs of food, and emergency seeds. CDoM have been supporting the emergency response to returnees from Sudan since the outset of the crisis in April 2023. They have been coordinating with the Cluster response mechanism and IOM, providing transport via boat for onward movement, emergency shelter NFIs and food assistance throughout 2023. Through coordination with the agencies active in the response, CDoM have continued to monitor needs and gaps in the response. A rapid needs assessment was conducted by Caritas Malakal at Malakal transit camp, in Fashoda-Kodok and Wadakona prior to planning for this emergency humanitarian response, where the beneficiaries had the lead in indicating their priority needs.
